_comment: fieldy 2026-11-26: the site uses MODERN (English) verse numbers everywhere unless something is completely dropped; a footer gives the Hebrew numbering. Joel (29) and Malachi (39) are now listed here like every other book (the old VERSIFICATION_MAP special case is retired). Entry kinds: a range {heb, engChapter, eng}; "merge": "end"|"start" = this Hebrew verse is FOLDED into English verse eng (after / before that verse's own Hebrew; its words follow on in one numbering); "words": [from, to] = only these word ordinals of the Hebrew verse (a split verse — Isaiah 63:19 = English 63:19 + 64:1), "pairs": [from, to) = which reading-text pairs of the Hebrew verse's text go to that English verse (checked by verify-site-verses). "added": English verses with no Hebrew at all, keyed book:chapter:verse, with the parallel they come from (Nehemiah 7:68 = Ezra 2:66). ONE reader for the pipeline: eng-versification.cjs; server.js builds its segments from the same file. History below. Known Hebrew (BHS/Masoretic) vs. English (KJV-tradition) chapter/verse numbering divergences, for the OT (canon_id 1-39). Keyed by "canon_id:hebChapter" — canon_id here means Scheme A per CLAUDE.md's 'book_id means two different things' note (stable 1-39 for OT, Genesis=1..Malachi=39), the SAME numbering tokens_bhs.book_id, resolveChapter()'s bookId, and VERSIFICATION_MAP already use — NOT the site's interspersed book-menu position numbers. Each entry is a list of verse-range correspondences for that Hebrew chapter; a single Hebrew chapter can span parts of two different English chapters (e.g. Numbers 17). Malachi (39) and Joel (29) are intentionally excluded — they're already special-cased in server.js's VERSIFICATION_MAP/DISPLAY_LAST_CHAPTER to DISPLAY English chapter numbers directly, so there's no divergence left to note about for those two. Psalms (19) are intentionally excluded — the offset there is systematic (most psalm titles count as verse 1 in Hebrew) and needs verification against which superscriptions this corpus's own tokens_bhs actually stores as verse 1 before any mapping can be trusted; flagged as follow-up work, not guessed at here. Source: standard, well-established Hebrew/English versification-difference table (matthewbarron.org's versification comparison, following the standard scholarly/SWORD-project convention). Spot-checked live against bldbible.com vs. biblehub.com for Deuteronomy 13 (2026-08-18) before this file was written; a few more entries should be spot-checked the same way before this is fully trusted (see verify step in the implementation). SPECIAL CASE — 1 Samuel 21 ("9:21"): unlike every other entry, this is NOT a clean 1-for-1 renumber. Per matthewbarron.org, Hebrew 20:42 and Hebrew 21:1 are two distinct Hebrew verses that English tradition folds into ONE English verse, 20:42 ("1Sa 20:42 (last clause)" = Hebrew 21:1). The heb[1,1]->eng20:[42,42] segment is flagged "merge": true so consuming code knows this destination is EXPECTED to already be occupied by Hebrew 20:42's own (unmoved) data — migrate-versification-translations.mjs has explicit merge-resolution logic for this flag (keep whichever side has real, non-baseline content; abort for manual review if both sides do). Confirmed 2026-08-20 against matthewbarron.org directly (not just spot-checked) after the migration script's collision guard caught this and "9:24" as genuine gaps in an earlier version of this file — 9:24 was a simple missing boundary segment (Hebrew 24:1 = English 23:29, no merge), fixed the same way as every other multi-segment entry.

16:7:68.note: Not in the Hebrew of Nehemiah 7: English Bibles add it from Ezra 2:66, the same list (horses 736, mules 245).
